learning_outcomes.text: Is able to present, defend, and discuss in public and in English, papers, reports, data, and conclusions professionally in the field of engineering and business.
Manage conflicts within work teams applying negotiation strategies.
Address negotiations in professional environments using verbal courtesy and argumentation strategies.

syllabus_topics: Unit 4 – Science - How do the laws of science affect our lives?
Unit 5 – Nutritional Science - How has science changed the food we eat?
Unit 6 – Education - Is one road to success better than other?
Unit 7 – Anthropology - How can accidental discoveries affect our lives?
Unit 8 – Engineering - What are the consequences of progress?
teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts related to the subjects and problem-solving, as well as in-person group sessions such as discussion classes and sharing.
Laboratory activities of increasing difficulty to acquire autonomy in problem-solving.
Personal study, report writing, practical assignments, etc., as independent work by the student or group of students.

assessment_methods.method: Class work (behavior/attitude, attendance, active participation, task completion)

assessment_rules: Students are evaluated through continuous assessment. This includes two written tests (25% each), two oral presentations (20% each), and class work (10%). If a student fails any partial test or does not take it, the ordinary call exam will be worth 100%, consisting of a 50% listening comprehension and vocabulary test and a 50% oral presentation. If the overall average grade in any continuous assessment test is below 2.5, the final grade will be a maximum of 3, and the student must take the ordinary call exam. For ordinary and extraordinary calls without continuous assessment, the evaluation consists of a 50% listening comprehension and vocabulary test and a 50% oral presentation.
